Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates bilateral, predominantly basal reticular and reticulonodular opacities with some volume loss, a pattern characteristic of interstitial lung disease (such as fibrosis) rather than the hyperinflation of COPD/Asthma or the upper-lobe cavitation of TB. In the context of the provided options and symptoms (fever, cough, dyspnea), this radiographic appearance is most consistent with an immunosuppression-related lung disease (e.g., opportunistic infection like Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia or drug-induced pneumonitis).
